news: Trump issues 10-15 day deadline on Iran nuclear deal
reality_check: Trump deadlines in 1st term were extended (NK 2017). Described as 'not scientific' by sources. Diplomatic track active — Geneva round 3 scheduled Feb 26. But 2nd-term track record: 60-day deadline in April 2025 DID lead to strikes.
lesson: Deadline rhetoric creates the sharpest spikes in GEO. The 25pp move in 48h on a rhetorical statement (no new military action) is a textbook availability + narrative cascade. However, this deadline WAS accompanied by genuine military buildup, narrowing the gap vs pure rhetoric spikes.

news: Geneva round 2 produces 'agreement on guiding principles' + Iran counterproposal more flexible than expected
reality_check: Diplomatic progress is genuine — Iran offering to export half of HEU, restore IAEA inspections, additional protocol. This is significantly more flexible than pre-talks position. But market barely moved because conservatism bias + belief perseverance keep 'strike is coming' belief sticky.
compound_pattern: None — this is an underreaction to positive news, the mirror of the War Panic Premium
lesson: The negative-positive asymmetry is stark: hawkish rhetoric moved prices 25pp in 48h; dovish diplomatic signals moved prices 3pp in 72h. An 8:1 ratio. This asymmetry is Loss Aversion (#11) manifesting in market dynamics. S004 should weight positive diplomatic signals MORE heavily than the market does as reversion catalysts.

news: SOTU 2026 — Trump uses 'Golden Age' framing, omits rally language
emotional_response: Surprise for retail (no MAGA, no Fake News). Validation for transcript analysts.
reality_check: MAGA has NEVER appeared in any Trump SOTU transcript (2017-2025). 'Fake News' has NEVER appeared. The 87% and 52% prices were pure identity-protective cognition + rally/formal confusion. Anyone who read SOTU transcripts had a 52pp and 37pp edge.
compound_pattern: Partisan Echo Chamber — identity-protective cognition prevented belief updating even though historical evidence was freely available
trade: Retrospective only — SOTU occurred before we could trade it
lesson: The SOTU ≠ Rally principle produced the single largest documented gap in our entire system (52pp). Identity-Protective Cognition (#8) is the most powerful bias in POL markets — it gets WORSE with participant sophistication, meaning informed Trump supporters were MORE confident MAGA would appear, not less. Our edge: reading transcripts vs. watching rallies.

news: Hot core PCE 3.0% kills March Fed cut thesis; FOMC minutes show hawks want hikes
emotional_response: Low emotion — processed analytically by professional participants
market: Will Fed decrease rates by 25bps after March 2026 meeting
market_move: -1.5pp (from 4.5% to 2.35%) + our entry at 2.85% exited at 2.35%
reality_check: The PCE data was genuinely informative. March cut probability was correctly near-zero. CME-Polymarket divergence closed in the WRONG direction for us — CME dropped to match Poly, not vice versa. Prediction markets can be MORE efficient than traditional derivatives on tail probabilities.
compound_pattern: None — this was NOT an emotional overreaction. ECI 3.3 correctly classified as structural.
lesson: T13: Cross-market divergence can close in wrong direction. T14: Asymmetric lottery tickets need constant probability re-evaluation. T15: Early entry exposes to thesis-killing data. CRITICAL VALIDATION: The ECI framework WORKS — ECI 3.3 < 4 should have flagged this as 'do not fade.' Had we applied the ECI trigger rule, we would have skipped T004 entirely.

news: SOTU 2026 — Trump omits 'China' despite 93% market price for mention
emotional_response: Surprise. China was the most salient geopolitical topic but was strategically omitted.
market: Will Trump mention China during SOTU (geography)
reality_check: Diplomatic calendar: March 31 China visit planned. Pre-visit protocol means avoiding antagonism. Trump did this before — minimal China mentions in 2018 SOTU during trade negotiations. Pattern: Trump is MORE hostile to countries he's NOT negotiating with. Our 75% estimate was better than market (18pp edge) but still directionally wrong.
compound_pattern: Availability (#1) + Salience (#2) — China tensions were the most available/salient geopolitical topic, making 'mention' feel near-certain. But diplomatic calendar overrides availability.
lesson: L02: Strategic omissions are predictable via diplomatic calendar. The China market was the biggest dollar mispricing ($93 vs $0 outcome). Edge source: diplomatic calendar analysis — a Category A5 signal applied to a Category B6 market. For future SOTU/speech markets: check which countries have upcoming Trump meetings/visits = lower mention probability.

news: Trump 2028 GOP nomination at 2.8% YES despite 22nd Amendment prohibition
emotional_response: Tribal wishful thinking — Trump supporters can't accept his candidacy is constitutionally impossible
market: Will Trump win 2028 Republican presidential nomination
market_move: Persistent 2-3% YES price (no spike — chronic mispricing)
speed: N/A — this is a steady-state mispricing, not an event-driven one
reality_check: The 22nd Amendment unambiguously prohibits a third term. No serious legal pathway exists. The 2.8% YES price implies either: (a) 2.8% chance the Constitution is amended (requires 2/3 Congress + 3/4 states), or (b) pure noise/identity trading. Neither justifies the price. True probability: <0.5%.
compound_pattern: Lottery Ticket Illusion — identity-attached hope premium + probability weighting (0.5% weighted as 2.8% = 5.6x overweighting, consistent with Tversky & Kahneman 1992 prediction for this probability level)
lesson: Constitutional impossibility premium is a PURE psychological phenomenon. There is no informational uncertainty — the 22nd Amendment is unambiguous. The entire 2.8% price is bias. This makes it the cleanest validation of probability weighting theory in our portfolio: a 0.5% event priced at 2.8% (5.6x overweight) matches the Prelec weighting function prediction almost exactly.

news: B05 Source Bias Audit — Gulf-state perspective missing from Iran positions
emotional_response: Analytical — no emotional spike, structural gap identified
market: US strikes Iran by March 31 / US or Israel strikes Iran by March 31
market_move: N/A — this is a source audit, not an event
reality_check: Gulf-state sources (Al Arabiya, Al-Monitor, Qatar media) show MORE diplomatic flexibility than Western media frames: Iran willing to dilute HEU, IRGC denying Hormuz exercises, Turkey FM confirms US tolerating enrichment boundaries, all 5 Gulf states denied base access and actively mediating. These dovish signals are underweighted in Western-sourced estimates.
compound_pattern: Source Concentration Bias — 3 Iran positions ($900 exposure) all sourced from Western military/diplomatic media (TWZ, Reuters, NYT). Gulf perspective systematically absent despite Gulf states being the most directly affected non-combatant parties.
trade: T003 revised from 52% to 49% YES; T005 revised from 55% to 52% YES
lesson: T16: Gulf-state media (Al Arabiya, Al-Monitor) provides essential dovish counterweight to Western military media on Iran. Gulf states have proximity intelligence and direct stake in non-escalation. Their reporting on diplomatic flexibility is systematically more detailed than Western sources. Source diversity protocol: ALWAYS include Al-Monitor + one Gulf state source for GEO/Middle East positions.
